Questions:

Could Player B play Deflection at this time (assuming he's already lost 1 pool?)

You can.
Because your predator's acting minion played an action modifier, you have
the right to answer with a reaction card before the bleed is succesful.
The pool is not really removed until when the bleed action is succesful.

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Kenneth Kristiansen wrote:

> Well... You can play deflection/redirection at any given time. Even after
> letting the bleed get through.

You can play reaction cards after you decline to block. Much like your
opponent can play action modifers after you decline to block.

>
> I'm not sure if you could play any reaction cards after physically removing
> blood from your pool...

You can't. But you don't actually remove blood from your pool until the
action resolves. The action does not resolve until both players are happy
with the action and no one has anymore cards to play.

>
> If you're beeing bled for one and you agree on that, how can the bleed be
> modified?? I always thought that bleed modifiers had to be played prior to
> removing any blood from the pool...

You can say "Ok. I don't block. I'm being bled for one", but your opponent
still has an opportunity to play action modifiers after you decline to block
but before the action resolves. Once the action resolves, you remove blood
from your pool. Before the action resolves, however, either player can play
modifiers and reactions.

Basically, you ask for blocks. Once you have resolved that no one is
blocking, you hit a point where you can't block anymore but you can still
play modifiers and reactions. Once both players have no cards to play, then
the action resolves.

If you say "I take the bleed for 1" or whatever, and then your opponent
plays Conditioning, you can then play a reaction (like Deflection or
something). You can't go back and try and block, as the time to declare
blockers has ended, but you can always play reactions or modifiers until the
action resolves.

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Itamar G. Jr. wrote:

> Player A Bleeds Player B
> Player B says "I'll not block"
> Player A says "So, it's one pool"
> Player B looses 1 pool
> Player A plays bonding (or any other bleed modifier)
>
> Questions:
>
> Could Player B play Deflection at this time (assuming he's already lost 1
> pool?)

In a sense. Player A can't play Bonding after player B loses one pool, but
he can play Bonding after Player B says "I'll take the bleed for 1", but
then player B can still play Deflection.

You don't actually lose pool until the action resolves. Once the action is
resolving, it is too late to play modifiers or reactions. However, before
the action resolves, either player can play modifiers or reaction cards. The
action doesn't resolve until both players are done playing modifiers or
reactions.

So in your example, what actually happens is:

Player A bleeds player B
Player B declines to block
Player A says "I'll take the bleed of 1"
Player B plays Bonding
Player A then can play Deflection or not.
After both players are done playing cards, the action resolves. Once the
action resolves, it is too late to play any other cards.

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
"Peter D Bakija" <PD...@bigplanet.com> wrote in message
news:B9185A9F.3740%PD...@bigplanet.com...

> Itamar G. Jr. wrote:
>
> > Player A Bleeds Player B
> > Player B says "I'll not block"
> > Player A says "So, it's one pool"
> > Player B looses 1 pool
> > Player A plays bonding (or any other bleed modifier)
> >

> So in your example, what actually happens is:
>
> Player A bleeds player B
> Player B declines to block
> Player A says "I'll take the bleed of 1"
> Player B plays Bonding
> Player A then can play Deflection or not.
> After both players are done playing cards, the action resolves. Once the
> action resolves, it is too late to play any other cards.
>

Actually, it looks to me like what happens is:

Player A bleeds player B.
Player B declines to block.
Player A declines to play any more action modifiers (says, "it's a bleed for
1.")
Player B declines to play any more reactions (begins removing blood from his
pool)

At this point, player A wants to play an action modifier, but it is too late.
He effectively gave up his chance when he said that the bleed was only for 1.
If, however, player B had reacted in anyway, player A would have another chance
to play action modifiers, but if both players pass sequentially, there's no
chance to play effects.

In a friendly game, player A would be allowed to play action modifiers here.
In a tournament, I would probably call a judge over, but it's 50-50 which way
he would rule. So, the answer to the original question is basically that yes
player A can play more action modifiers, but according to strict interpretation
of the rules, it is too late.

A bleeds, B declares he's not going to block with his only untapped minion,
A modifies his bleed for 3 and B deflects him.
But all other players deflect the bleed, so A comes back to bleed B: since

with another vamp (I guess no because he already declared he would have not
blocked)?
Can he play a 2nd Trad (I think it's different from a Wake because the card
states that you have to block)?

Yes. Changing the target of the bleed (or other action) results in a new
"choose blockers" stage.

> Can he play a 2nd Trad (I think it's different from a Wake because the card
> states that you have to block)?

It's no different in that he can still use it to block.
If he couldn't wake and block, he couldn't 2ndTrad and block, either.
